verdict.root_cause: Every cart operation is paying a fixed ~300ms penalty on its call to the cart backing store. Traces at 11:21 show cartservice's redis child spans (HGET, HMSET) consuming ~301-307ms of self time each while the cartservice handler contributes under 1ms, and latency scales linearly with the number of redis round-trips (~305ms for one op, ~610ms for two, ~665ms for checkout's GetCart+EmptyCart) [tr_3984cc69c503]. The tight clustering at a ~300ms floor with no heavy tail is the signature of a fixed per-operation delay inserted into the network path, not server-side contention. The cartservice change log independently records a traffic-shaping container attached to the cart-service network namespace adding fixed egress delay on eth0, applied and reverted in repeating cycles by platform-automation [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8]. Nothing is erroring at the cart layer [tr_5f846f914e7b][tr_3984cc69c503]. checkoutservice is a victim: its dominant latency is the cartservice redis hops [tr_17013007cead], its success path slowed from ~20-25ms to ~600-650ms per order [tr_b00c5e027670], and its 1.1%-mean/6.7%-peak error ratio [tr_90d42a699f94] fits a small fraction of requests tipping over a client deadline. The mechanism is a slow dependency call path on cartservice's cart-store egress; the service failed because it waited.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent trace dispatches put essentially all wall time in cartservice's redis spans and exonerate every other hop, including frontend/gRPC transport and payment, currency, productcatalog, shipping and email [tr_3984cc69c503][tr_17013007cead]. The delay is additive per redis operation and identical for reads and writes, excluding application logic and write-only faults [tr_3984cc69c503]. A uniform ~300ms floor with no errors or connection failures [tr_5f846f914e7b] matches an injected network delay, and the change log names exactly that artifact on the cart namespace [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8]. checkoutservice's symptoms follow: no recorded changes in 24h [tr_c0db7cb47df3], errors from a flat-zero baseline but under 7% - too low for a hard outage [tr_90d42a699f94] - and an intact but ~25x slower success path [tr_b00c5e027670]. The image apply/revert pairs put no hotfix artifact in effect at onset [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8], so removing the injected egress delay, not a rollback, is the fix.
open_questions: The change log shows every traffic-shaping container reverted, the latest ~1.6h before onset, and nothing in the hour before onset [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8], yet traces at 11:21 show the delay [tr_3984cc69c503]; whether an injection cycle went unrecorded or a revert failed to take effect is unsettled and decides whether config_revert is an available lever.

No evidence was gathered from the cart backing store itself - no redis-cart metrics, logs, or change history - so a genuine server-side ~300ms stall was excluded only by latency shape, not direct observation.

The source of checkoutservice's errors is inferred: no span carries an error status [tr_17013007cead] and the checkout log slice was truncated past the ~11:00 onset [tr_b00c5e027670], so no failing RPC or status code was named; cartservice's own error ratio is unmeasurable due to an empty calls_total series [tr_235ca2bc63c4].

alternatives.root_cause: The cart backing store (redis-cart) is itself slow, adding ~300ms to every HGET/HMSET server-side.
alternatives.why_not: Redis was never directly observed, but a genuinely loaded store produces a heavy-tailed spread, not the tight ~301-307ms clustering seen identically on reads and writes [tr_3984cc69c503]; a fixed injected delay is recorded in the change log [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8] and explains the floor exactly.

alternatives.root_cause: A stale REDIS_ADDR override left cartservice pointed at a non-default redis endpoint whose path is slower.
alternatives.why_not: Both REDIS_ADDR updates have paired reverts to unset, the latest ~1.3h before onset [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8], and a wrong endpoint would more likely yield connection errors than a clean uniform delay; cart logs show no connection failures [tr_5f846f914e7b].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in observables is expected. The ~300ms floor on cartservice's HGET/HMSET self-times and the ~650ms checkout end-to-end will persist until the injected egress delay is removed by whoever owns the injecting automation. If an injection cycle ends on its own, redis child-span self-time should drop back under ~5ms and checkoutservice's error ratio should return to a flat zero without any action from this system - which is itself the observation that would show the cause was the transient shaping cycle.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if a standing configuration on cartservice is in fact carrying the delay. That would show up as a REDIS_ADDR or image override still present in cartservice's live environment with no matching revert - the change log says the opposite, that every apply has a paired revert and the latest is ~1.6h before onset [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8]. It would also be wrong if direct observation of redis-cart (never gathered: no metrics, logs, or change history for the backing store) showed a genuine server-side ~300ms stall, since that is a different mechanism from the one the verdict names and none of the permitted actions target redis-cart anyway.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the latency continues: every cart read and write keeps paying ~300ms, checkout stays at ~650ms per order, and the 1.1%-mean/6.7%-peak checkoutservice error ratio [tr_90d42a699f94] keeps shedding a small fraction of orders for as long as the injection cycle runs. That is a real cost and it is accepted deliberately, because the alternatives are worse: revert_config's preconditions are not met - the mechanism is a traffic-shaping container attached to the cart-service network namespace, not a value in cartservice's environment, and the change log records no configuration change inside the incident window at all (nearest is a revert ~1.3h before onset) [tr_8c23c4d6c8e8]. Restoring a prior environment would recreate cartservice while changing nothing about the egress qdisc, dropping every in-flight cart RPC and its cache for no mechanistic gain, and could even re-apply a REDIS_ADDR override pointing at a non-default port. rollback_image is ruled out by the same evidence: the hotfix image was reverted ~1.9h before onset, so there is no bad image live to roll back. restart_service requires evidence of process state, and the evidence says the opposite - cartservice logs are clean and continuous through 11:22 with no panic or restart lines [tr_5f846f914e7b] and its handler self-time is under 1ms [tr_3984cc69c503]. scale_service is unavailable per ADR-0029.
proposal.blast_radius: No service is touched, so nobody sees a change from this system. The ongoing incident continues to be visible to cartservice's callers - frontend on the cart read/add path and checkoutservice on GetCart+EmptyCart [tr_17013007cead] - and through frontend to loadgenerator. The correct next step is outside this system's permitted actions: identify the owner of the platform-automation injection cycles and have the traffic-shaping container on the cart-service network namespace removed, and gather direct evidence from redis-cart to close the open question about a server-side stall.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerting near-simultaneously with cartservice first and checkoutservice/frontend following fits downstream propagation from the cart path, not a single quiet warning. No open incident covers it, so it warrants investigation.
